snippet.title: The IMPOSSIBLE Choice: ₹3 Lakh Phone Vs ₹3 Lakh CAR! Cheapest Indian Car Right Now #shorts
snippet.description:
Apple’s iPhone Duo has prompted a striking price comparison for Indian buyers. The 1TB model is listed at ₹3,74,900 on Apple’s India store. Maruti Suzuki lists the base S-Presso at ₹3,49,900 ex-showroom. On those listed prices, the phone costs ₹25,000 more than the starting price of the car.

The comparison captures how expensive premium smartphones have become.

Apple introduced the iPhone Duo in India with storage options from 256GB to 2TB. Its entry-level price is ₹2,99,900, while the 1TB configuration is one of its costlier choices. That makes the S-Presso comparison specific to this storage variant, rather than every iPhone Duo model.

For Indian consumers, the contrast is memorable because a phone and an entry-level car serve entirely different needs. One is a portable device with a limited upgrade cycle; the other provides transport but brings continuing expenses such as fuel, maintenance and insurance.

The figures do not tell anyone which purchase makes more sense. They do show how far flagship phone pricing has moved: at ₹3.75 lakh, a high-storage smartphone can now sit alongside an affordable car in a buyer’s budget discussion.

snippet.title: 7,000 Kmph Speed! The 'Scary Dance' Missile of India - PRALAY - Indian Army & DRDO #shorts
snippet.description:
India’s indigenously developed Pralay missile has moved closer to military induction after a successful flight test off the Odisha coast on November 5. The Defence Research and Development Organisation said the test met all its objectives. Conducted as part of user evaluation trials, it was monitored using instruments at the Integrated Test Range.

Pralay is described as a quasi-ballistic missile. Unlike a conventional ballistic missile following a more predictable arc, it can fly on a lower trajectory and manoeuvre during flight. That ability has prompted descriptions of the missile “dancing” through the sky, although its movements are controlled by its guidance system, not random. Changing course can make a missile more challenging for an opponent to track and intercept.

The trial has also revived comparisons with BrahMos. The two missiles serve different roles: Pralay is a tactical surface-to-surface weapon designed to carry conventional warheads, while BrahMos is a supersonic cruise missile available for several launch platforms. BrahMos’s manufacturer lists its cruise speed at around Mach 2.8. Reports describe Pralay reaching higher speeds during parts of its ballistic-style flight, but that does not mean it sustains a faster cruising speed than BrahMos throughout its journey.

Research Centre Imarat in Hyderabad developed Pralay with other DRDO laboratories, while Bharat Dynamics Limited is a production partner. The Defence Ministry said the latest result makes induction imminent; it did not announce that the missile is already in operational service.

For India, the significance lies in adding a domestically developed option to its conventional strike capabilities. Pralay’s manoeuvrable flight path and BrahMos’s sustained supersonic cruise offer different capabilities rather than a simple contest over which missile is “better.”

snippet.description:
A routine LPG cylinder delivery in Bengaluru turned into a frightening incident when escaping gas caught fire near a lit diya. The fire broke out at a home in the Malleshwaram area, and video of the delivery worker’s narrow escape circulated widely. 

The footage shows the worker placing the cylinder near the doorway and removing its safety cap. A hissing sound can be heard before flames erupt beside an oil lamp at the entrance. Police accounts suggest leaking gas reached the flame.

The incident has particular relevance for Indian households, where diyas and incense are often placed near entrances during prayers and festivals. Even a small flame can ignite escaping LPG. Keeping delivery and installation areas clear of open flames gives workers room to check a cylinder safely.

IndianOil’s safety guidance says anyone who smells gas should turn off the regulator if it is safe to do so, extinguish nearby flames and open doors and windows. Electrical switches should not be turned on or off because they may produce a spark. 

The Bengaluru video is a reminder that LPG safety begins before a cylinder is connected: the surrounding area must be checked for ignition sources, and any suspected leak needs prompt professional attention.

snippet.title: TRAIN Driver RECORDED 'Scariest Moment of His Life' - Kolkata Sairang Express Derail #shorts
snippet.description:
A video said to have been recorded inside a locomotive moments before a train derailed in Assam has raised questions about its braking system. The Kolkata–Sairang Express derailed near Digaru railway station, outside Guwahati, at around 6:54 am on November 11. The locomotive and five coaches went off the tracks.

In the circulating footage, a crew member can be heard saying that the brakes, including the emergency brake, had been applied but the train was not stopping. The video appears to end as the locomotive strikes the end of the track.

The railway’s initial statement said the loco pilot could not control the train’s speed as it entered Digaru to allow another service to pass. That describes what happened before the derailment; it does not establish why the train failed to stop. Some experienced loco pilots examining the video have also questioned a spoken description of the brake-pipe gauge. A technical investigation is needed to determine whether there was a brake malfunction, another equipment issue or a different cause.

Following the accident, railway teams carried out relief work and arranged another train for stranded passengers. Services on the affected section were subsequently restored.

For Indian rail passengers, the footage makes the final moments of the incident especially concerning. The crucial finding will come from the formal examination of the train’s systems and crew actions, rather than conclusions drawn from a short viral clip.

snippet.title: Sánchez espera que el voto de González "pase del blanco al rojo" para frenar a la derecha
snippet.description:
El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, ha manifestado este jueves su intención de convencer al expresidente Felipe González para que cambie su postura de cara a la votación del próximo 29 de noviembre. Sánchez espera poder ofrecerle argumentos suficientes para que su voto pase «del blanco al rojo», en referencia a la posibilidad de que González vote en blanco. El actual jefe del Ejecutivo ha defendido que esta opción no contribuye a frenar a la derecha y ha insistido en la importancia de apoyar al PSOE.

Durante una entrevista concedida al programa de Televisión Española (TVE) El perro andaluz, Sánchez ha abordado las críticas que Felipe González ha dirigido contra su gestión al frente del Gobierno y su decisión de no respaldar al partido en la próxima cita electoral. El expresidente socialista ha anunciado públicamente su intención de votar en blanco, una postura que ha generado reacciones dentro de la formación.Preguntado por esta cuestión, Sánchez ha mostrado su disposición a dialogar con González y tratar de hacerle cambiar de opinión.

El presidente ha recordado, además, la influencia que tuvo el histórico dirigente socialista en sus propios comienzos políticos. Según ha explicado, una de las razones que le llevaron a afiliarse al PSOE fue precisamente la admiración que sentía por Felipe González y por su trayectoria política.De esta manera, Sánchez ha apelado tanto a la historia compartida como a la responsabilidad política del expresidente para intentar acercar posturas. Su mensaje pone de manifiesto las diferencias existentes entre ambos dirigentes, especialmente en relación con la situación actual del partido y las decisiones que debe tomar el socialismo ante las próximas elecciones.El presidente considera que el voto en blanco no es una solución para frenar a la derecha y confía en que González pueda reconsiderar su decisión antes del 29N.

snippet.title: How They Transformed a 300-Year-Old Haveli Into a Luxury Home | India
snippet.description:
Khohar Haveli, an 18th-century heritage mansion near Sohna, Haryana, in the foothills of the Aravalli Hills, is owned and cared for by the Yogi Vaid family. With its rich history, traditional architecture and thoughtful restoration, this 300 years old haveli tells a story of preserving the past while bringing it into the present.

In this episode of FramexFrame, we explore Khohar Haveli’s carved arches, old doorways, peaceful courtyards and beautifully restored rooms. Blending historic Indian architecture with modern comforts, the haveli offers a glimpse into a different way of living, where old-world charm meets understated luxury.

The story of the haveli also connects with Aman Nath, co-founder of Neemrana Hotels, who helped restore the property and bring new life to its historic spaces. Traditional building methods, local craftsmanship and carefully chosen furnishings helped preserve the character of this remarkable heritage home.

The property later came into the hands of Yogi Vaid, a childhood friend of Aman Nath. Today, the Vaid family continues to preserve the haveli’s rich heritage, with Yogi Vaid’s son, Ambar Vaid, and daughter-in-law, Shafiqua Gulri, involved in its upkeep and restoration. The property is now managed by StayVista, bringing together its historic charm and the comforts of a luxury heritage stay.

More than just a heritage stay, Khohar Haveli is a living piece of India’s architectural past. Join FramexFrame as we discover historic homes, traditional architecture, heritage properties and hidden places with stories worth telling.
